pages.scan: I opened the request JSON and looked at works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/review/page-03.png with Read. The page has five panels in the same layout as the storyboard. Reading left to right, top to bottom: (1) Top-left panel, caption at the top left: "A later morning: patients can always check in at the front desk." An elderly man (white hair, glasses, cream short-sleeved shirt, wooden cane) stands at the reception counter and smiles at a young receptionist (dark braid, blue patterned kurta) who is typing and smiling back. This is a silent friendly greeting. Behind them are a QR stand by the window, waiting chairs with two seated patients, and a teal wall screen. (2) Top-right panel, caption at the top: "Some check in ahead on the Welbuk Health app." Outside the clinic's glass entrance, a young woman (dark ponytail with a blue tie, earrings, coral kurta with a leaf pattern, navy crossbody bag) smiles as she taps her phone; the screen shows a calendar or check-in icon. Silent. (3) Middle-left panel, caption at the top left: "Ravi scans the QR code at the door." A bearded man (sage-green button shirt, brown shoulder-bag strap, wristwatch on his left wrist) holds his phone up to a QR stand and looks at it. In the background are the receptionist at the desk and, seen from behind in the waiting chairs, the elderly man and the woman in coral. Silent. (4) Middle-right panel, caption at the top left: "A short form on his own phone, shared with consent." A close-up shows Ravi's hands with the watch on the phone, which displays form fields and a check mark, and his profile looks down at it calmly. Silent. (5) Wide bottom panel. First the caption at the top left: "Every check-in gets a slot on the screen." Then the label on the wall screen at the upper right: "A-10 · A-11 · A-12". Below it the elderly man with his cane, the woman in coral holding her phone and Ravi holding his phone with a brown bag on his lap sit side by side. All three look up toward the screen with content smiles. This is a silent closing reaction.
pages.observation: The reading order is unambiguous: the page has five captions, each at the top left of its panel, and the only other text is the screen label, which is read last. The page has no speech balloons, so no reply can be skipped. All text is legible, including "Welbuk Health" and "A-10 · A-11 · A-12". The screen label sits on top of the drawn TV screen, so it reads as what the screen shows. Coverage: none of the captions covers a face or a hand. In panel 1 the caption box overlaps the left part of the teal wall screen, which is a background object and harmless. In panel 2 the caption box ends just above the top of the woman's ponytail with very little clearance, but it does not cover her. In panel 3 the right and bottom edges of the caption box come very close to, and may slightly clip, the top-left edge of Ravi's hair; this is minor and worth a look. In panel 4 the caption sits clear of the phone and of Ravi's face. Continuity: the elderly man has the same white hair, glasses, cream shirt and cane in panels 1, 3 (background) and 5. The receptionist has the same braid and blue kurta in panels 1 and 3 (background). The woman has the same ponytail with blue tie, coral leaf-pattern kurta, navy crossbody bag and phone in panels 2, 3 (from behind) and 5. Ravi has the same beard, sage-green shirt, brown bag or strap and left-wrist watch in panels 3, 4 and 5. Minor ambiguities: (a) the caption says the QR code is "at the door", but in panel 3 the QR stand is drawn inside near the reception counter and waiting area, and in panel 1 one stands by the window, so "at the door" does not quite match the picture; (b) in panel 5 nothing shows which of A-10, A-11 and A-12 belongs to which person, although the left-to-right seating suggests the order; (c) the receptionist from panel 1 is not named on this page, which does not hurt comprehension. I found no blocking reading-order problems; the possible hair clip in panel 3 and the door/QR mismatch are small issues to consider.
